title: Why do we wash our hands?
lines: Sam is four years old and he's always in a hurry.
With his cars, with his blocks and outside in the sandpit.
And there's one thing he hates: washing his hands.
Why do I always have to do that?
One morning Sam is playing in the garden.
He picks up a snail and looks at it really closely.
He wants to sit down at the table straight away.
There are pancakes on the table!
There's a bit of soil under his nails, but otherwise they look fine.
There are tiny little creatures on your hands.
They're so small that you can't see them.
Not even with your very best eyes.
Those little creatures are called bacteria.
They're too small to see, says Daddy.
But some can make you ill.
Then you get a tummy ache, or a runny nose, or a fever.
And if you eat a pancake with dirty hands, the little creatures go right in with it.
Then he looks at his hands.
I don't want to eat creatures.
He takes a little plate of water.
He sprinkles a little pepper on it.
The black pepper floats on the water.
Pretend that pepper is the little creatures.
Put your finger in the water.
Sam puts his finger in the water.
The pepper sticks to his finger.
Now put a little soap on your finger.
And then put it in the water again.
Sam puts a drop of soap on his finger.
He puts his finger in the water.
All the pepper shoots away, to the edge of the plate.
The creatures are running away from the soap!
Soap is very strong against creatures.
That's why we wash our hands.
Come on, I'll show you how.
They go to the sink together.
First you wet your hands, says Daddy.
And under your nails, where the soil is.
For as long as it takes to sing the birthday song twice, says Daddy.
Happy birthday to you, happy birthday to you.
He sings it twice, really loudly.
Then you rinse it all off with water.
Sam sees the brown water running away.
And then you dry your hands on the towel.
The pancakes are delicious, with sugar and a little lemon.
When else do I have to wash my hands?
asks Sam with his mouth full.
And when you've sneezed into your hands.
But it's fun with the song.
From that day on Sam washes his hands really well.
And when his little sister Lien doesn't want to wash her hands, Sam says: Lien, there are creatures on them!
Come on, I'll show you the pepper experiment.
